MODEL_FEEDBACK_JSON:
{
  "positive_alignment_reasons": [
    "The lag bolts feel like a natural addition to my screw and bolt kits because they cover heavier wood fastening jobs that my smaller hardware may not handle.",
    "The E-clips and snap rings fit the same practical repair needs as my cotter pins and rivet nuts: having several sizes available helps when a repair needs a particular fastener. I would choose the E-clips now and leave the snap rings for a specific need."
  ],
  "negative_misalignment_reasons": [
    "The test leads, heat shrink tubing, and harness tape assume I have a wiring project underway, but my recent purchases give me more reason to choose fastening and fabrication supplies today.",
    "My adhesive and mounting tapes solve bonding problems; gaffers tape serves a different purpose, so being another tape does not make it useful to me right now.",
    "The pressure gauge requires a pressure-testing task and a compatible fitting, while the ultrasonic cleaner needs enough recurring cleaning work to justify a dedicated machine. Neither fills a current need for me."
  ],
  "overgeneralized_signals": [
    "Owning workshop tools seems to have been taken as a reason to offer electrical testing and wiring supplies, even though those require a different task.",
    "My interest in tapes and assorted supplies seems to have carried over too broadly. An assortment or a roll is useful only when its actual function matches the work I need to do."
  ],
  "missing_or_underweighted_signals": [
    "My repeated purchases of screws, bolts, rivets, rivet nuts, and cotter pins make complementary fastening hardware especially relevant.",
    "Specific sizes, fitting compatibility, and intended use matter to my choice. I would not choose a particular tubing size or threaded gauge just because it belongs in a workshop.",
    "Related repair supplies can still overlap in usefulness today: liking both retaining-clip assortments does not mean I need to choose both now."
  ],
  "summary_diagnosis": "The recommendations recognized my interest in repair hardware but stretched it into wiring, testing, and cleaning needs I do not currently have."
}
